trajectory_messages.content:
I'm working with the Elgato integration in Home Assistant and I've noticed that the error messages are both inaccurate and unhelpful.

*   When a connection error (ElgatoConnectionError) is raised during any Elgato entity operation (button press, light control, switch control), the integration must raise a HomeAssistantError whose message contains exactly: 'An error occurred while communicating with the Elgato device'

*   When a generic/unknown error (ElgatoError but not ElgatoConnectionError) is raised during any Elgato entity operation (button press, light control, switch control, identify), the integration must raise a HomeAssistantError whose message contains exactly: 'An unknown error occurred while communicating with the Elgato device'

*   Connection errors (ElgatoConnectionError) and generic errors (ElgatoError) must be handled separately and produce distinct error messages — the connection error message does not include 'unknown', while the generic error message includes 'unknown'

*   The button entity must handle both ElgatoConnectionError and ElgatoError when a button is pressed, raising the appropriate HomeAssistantError for each

*   The light entity must handle ElgatoConnectionError when controlling the light (turning on or off), raising a HomeAssistantError with the connection error message

*   The light entity must handle ElgatoError when identifying the light, raising a HomeAssistantError with the unknown error message

*   The switch entity must handle ElgatoError when turning the switch on or off, raising a HomeAssistantError with the unknown error message

*   Error messages must refer to 'Elgato device' (not 'Elgato Light') across all entity types including buttons, lights, and switches


**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.
I'll start by exploring the Elgato integration source files.

28	    hass: HomeAssistant,
29	    entry: ElgatoConfigEntry,

37	class ElgatoLight(ElgatoEntity, LightEntity):
38	    """Defines an Elgato Light."""
39	
40	    _attr_name = None
41	    _attr_min_color_temp_kelvin = 2900  # 344 Mireds
42	    _attr_max_color_temp_kelvin = 7000  # 143 Mireds
43	
44	    def __init__(self, coordinator: ElgatoDataUpdateCoordinator) -> None:
45	        """Initialize Elgato Light."""
46	        super().__init__(coordinator)
47	        self._attr_supported_color_modes = {ColorMode.COLOR_TEMP}
48	        self._attr_unique_id = coordinator.data.info.serial_number
49	
50	        # Elgato Light supporting color, have a different temperature range
51	        if (
52	            self.coordinator.data.info.product_name
53	            in (
54	                "Elgato Light Strip",
55	                "Elgato Light Strip Pro",
56	            )
57	            or self.coordinator.data.settings.power_on_hue
58	            or self.coordinator.data.state.hue is not None
59	        ):
60	            self._attr_supported_color_modes = {ColorMode.COLOR_TEMP, ColorMode.HS}
61	            self._attr_min_color_temp_kelvin = 3500  # 285 Mireds
62	            self._attr_max_color_temp_kelvin = 6500  # 153 Mireds
63	
64	    @property
65	    def brightness(self) -> int | None:
66	        """Return the brightness of this light between 1..255."""
67	        return round((self.coordinator.data.state.brightness * 255) / 100)
68	
69	    @property
70	    def color_temp_kelvin(self) -> int | None:
71	        """Return the color temperature value in Kelvin."""
72	        if (mired_temperature := self.coordinator.data.state.temperature) is None:
73	            return None
74	        return color_util.color_temperature_mired_to_kelvin(mired_temperature)
75	
76	    @property
77	    def color_mode(self) -> ColorMode:
78	        """Return the color mode of the light."""
79	        if self.coordinator.data.state.hue is not None:
80	            return ColorMode.HS
81	
82	        return ColorMode.COLOR_TEMP
83	
84	    @property
85	    def hs_color(self) -> tuple[float, float] | None:
86	        """Return the hue and saturation color value [float, float]."""
87	        return (
88	            self.coordinator.data.state.hue or 0,
89	            self.coordinator.data.state.saturation or 0,
90	        )
91	
92	    @property
93	    def is_on(self) -> bool:
94	        """Return the state of the light."""
95	        return self.coordinator.data.state.on
96	
97	    async def async_turn_off(self, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
98	        """Turn off the light."""
99	        try:
100	            await self.coordinator.client.light(on=False)
101	        except ElgatoError as error:
102	            raise HomeAssistantError(
103	                "An error occurred while updating the Elgato Light"
104	            ) from error
105	        finally:
106	            await self.coordinator.async_refresh()
107	
108	    async def async_turn_on(self, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
109	        """Turn on the light."""
110	        temperature_kelvin = kwargs.get(ATTR_COLOR_TEMP_KELVIN)
111	
112	        hue = None
113	        saturation = None
114	        if ATTR_HS_COLOR in kwargs:
115	            hue, saturation = kwargs[ATTR_HS_COLOR]
116	
117	        brightness = None
118	        if ATTR_BRIGHTNESS in kwargs:
119	            brightness = round((kwargs[ATTR_BRIGHTNESS] / 255) * 100)
120	
121	        # For Elgato lights supporting color mode, but in temperature mode;
122	        # adjusting only brightness make them jump back to color mode.
123	        # Resending temperature prevents that.
124	        if (
125	            brightness
126	            and ATTR_HS_COLOR not in kwargs
127	            and ATTR_COLOR_TEMP_KELVIN not in kwargs
128	            and self.supported_color_modes
129	            and ColorMode.HS in self.supported_color_modes
130	            and self.color_mode == ColorMode.COLOR_TEMP
131	        ):
132	            temperature_kelvin = self.color_temp_kelvin
133	
134	        temperature = (
135	            None
136	            if temperature_kelvin is None
137	            else color_util.color_temperature_kelvin_to_mired(temperature_kelvin)
138	        )
139	
140	        try:
141	            await self.coordinator.client.light(
142	                on=True,
143	                brightness=brightness,
144	                hue=hue,
145	                saturation=saturation,
146	                temperature=temperature,
147	            )
148	        except ElgatoError as error:
149	            raise HomeAssistantError(
150	                "An error occurred while updating the Elgato Light"
151	            ) from error
152	        finally:
153	            await self.coordinator.async_refresh()
154	
155	    async def async_identify(self) -> None:
156	        """Identify the light, will make it blink."""
157	        try:
158	            await self.coordinator.client.identify()
159	        except ElgatoError as error:
160	            raise HomeAssistantError(
161	                "An error occurred while identifying the Elgato Light"
162	            ) from error
